newsitem.title: USA: U.S. environmentalists sue over Grand Canyon rule.
newsitem.headline: U.S. environmentalists sue over Grand Canyon rule.

text.p: Seven conservation and outdoor groups Thursday sued the Federal Aviation Administration, saying its plan to reduce noisy air tour flights over the Grand Canyon was not enough to restore quiet to the national park.
Grand Canyon air tour operators sued the agency last week, complaining that the rules to reduce airspace and restrict flight hours were unjustified and will hurt their business.

"Ten years after Congress said future generations deserve to know what a quiet Canyon is like, the FAA still can't bring itself to comply with the law," Robert Wiygul, a Denver-based attorney for the Sierra Club Legal Defense Fund, said in a statement.
He was referring to the 1987 Overflights Act that directed the FAA and the U.S. Parks Service to take measures to restore quiet to the Grand Canyon.

The Clinton administration last month announced is rule to reduce allowable air space and impose dusk-to-dawn curfews on the tour flights, but the conservation groups complained the rule did not reduce the number of tour flights.
The Parks Service estimates there are 80,000-95,000 tour flights over the Grand Canyon annually.
Other groups in the suit were the National Parks and Conservation Association, the Wilderness Society and several Grand Canyon advocacy organizations.
